# Third-party notices

`Sources/ChronoForgeCore/SPC700.swift` and `SPC700ISA.swift` port the CPU and
opcode definitions from Gustavo Franco's
[sony-spc700-python](https://github.com/gufranco/sony-spc700-python/tree/91c0576a00bd7eae09847f8f34bd4ff2dfc46773),
commit `91c0576a00bd7eae09847f8f34bd4ff2dfc46773`. The MIT license is reproduced
in `sony-spc700-python-LICENSE`. `bundle_app.sh` includes this directory with
the compiled application and CLI.

`Sources/ChronoForgeCore/CTTextCodec.swift` adapts the Chrono Trigger text
mapping and compression rules from ChronoRET's `tools/text.py` (MIT, Copyright
(c) 2026 Akill). The license is reproduced in `ChronoRET-LICENSE`. No ROM data,
dictionary or game text is bundled; the codec reads them from the user's ROM.

The numerical instruction fixtures under `Tests/ChronoForgeCoreTests/Resources/SPC700`
are sampled from SingleStepTests/ProcessorTests, generated by David Schneider's
JSMoo. Their source commit, selection indices and checksum are recorded beside
the fixture. They contain no game ROM data and are not bundled with the app.
The pinned upstream commit carries no license file, so `vectors.json` is not
committed to the public repository; `tools/prepare_spc700_vectors.py` regenerates
it from a pinned checkout (CI does this at test time).
